description: A two-panel composite figure of line plots with point markers, both panels sharing the same categorical x-axis labelled "Samples" with four conditions in reading order: as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h. (a) plots "Average size (µm)" on a y-axis running 0.0 to 2.0 with gridlines every 0.5; (b) plots "Volume fraction (vol.%)" on a y-axis running 0.0 to 1.8 with gridlines every 0.6. Both panels carry an identical legend: black squares = "0.02Nb steels", red circles = "0.04Nb steels"; both data series in (a) show error bars, which are clearly visible on the red 0.04Nb curve. Both panels display the same two-fold trend: values rise monotonically with aging temperature from the as-cast condition to 823 K/3 h, and the 0.04Nb curve lies above the 0.02Nb curve at every condition. In (a) the 0.02Nb average size increases from just above the 0.5 µm gridline at as-cast to between the 1.0 and 1.5 µm gridlines at 823 K/3 h, while the 0.04Nb series reaches between 1.5 and 2.0 µm; in (b) the volume fraction rises from near the 0.0 line at as-cast to about the 0.6 vol.% gridline for 0.02Nb and midway between the 1.2 and 1.8 vol.% gridlines for 0.04Nb. No numeric data labels are printed, so values are read only against gridlines. The figure demonstrates that both the average size and the volume fraction of the NbC particles increase slightly with higher aging temperature and with higher Nb content.

subfigures.description: Line plot of "Average size (µm)" (y-axis 0.0-2.0, gridlines every 0.5) versus the categorical sample axis (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h). Two series with error bars: black squares "0.02Nb steels" and red circles "0.04Nb steels"; both rise monotonically with aging temperature, and 0.04Nb is higher than 0.02Nb at every condition, reaching between the 1.5 and 2.0 µm gridlines at 823 K/3 h.

Line plot of "Volume fraction (vol.%)" (y-axis 0.0-1.8, gridlines every 0.6) versus the same categorical sample axis. Same legend (black squares "0.02Nb steels", red circles "0.04Nb steels"). Volume fraction increases monotonically from near 0 at as-cast to about 0.6 vol.% (0.02Nb) and between 1.2 and 1.8 vol.% (0.04Nb) at 823 K/3 h, with the 0.04Nb curve consistently above the 0.02Nb curve.

observations.observation: Panel (a) y-axis is labelled "Average size (µm)" and spans 0.0 to 2.0 with gridlines at 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0.
Panel (b) y-axis is labelled "Volume fraction (vol.%)" and spans 0.0 to 1.8 with gridlines at 0.0, 0.6, 1.2 and 1.8.
Both panels share the categorical x-axis labelled "Samples" with four conditions: as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h.
The legend in both panels reads exactly "0.02Nb steels" (black squares) and "0.04Nb steels" (red circles).
In both panels the 0.04Nb curve lies above the 0.02Nb curve at all four sample conditions, and both curves increase monotonically with aging temperature.
Error bars are drawn on the data points of panel (a); their magnitudes are small and not numerically readable.
No numerical data labels are printed on either panel; values can only be read relative to the gridlines.
The caption states that panel (a) shows the average size and panel (b) the volume fraction of NbC particles in Nb-containing steels.
The citing text states that at least five SEM images of each sample were analysed with ImageJ software to obtain these statistics.

The citing text states that both the size and volume fraction of the NbC particles increase slightly with higher aging temperature and more Nb content, matching the two upward-trending curve pairs in this figure.
The citing text links Figure 4 with Figure 7, stating that the precipitation of NbC particles and κ-carbides is greatly influenced by both the Nb content and the aging treatments.
